options.text: A reaction that only goes in one direction
A reaction that can proceed in both the forward and backward directions
A reaction that cannot be started
A reaction that produces no products

questions.explanation: A reversible reaction is one that can proceed in both the forward direction (reactants to products) and the backward direction (products back to reactants).

questions.stem: Which symbol is used to represent a reversible reaction in a chemical equation?
questions.explanation: The ⇌ symbol (two half arrows pointing in opposite directions) is used to show that a reaction is reversible, indicating both forward and reverse reactions can occur.

questions.stem: Hydrated copper sulfate (blue) can be heated to form anhydrous copper sulfate (white) and water. When water is added to anhydrous copper sulfate, it turns blue again. What does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: This is a classic example of a reversible reaction. Heating drives the forward reaction (dehydration), while adding water drives the reverse reaction (hydration).

questions.stem: If the forward reaction in a reversible process is exothermic, what can be said about the reverse reaction?

options.text: It is endothermic by the same amount of energy
It releases more energy than the forward reaction

questions.explanation: In a reversible reaction, if the forward reaction is exothermic (releases energy), the reverse reaction is endothermic (absorbs energy) by exactly the same amount.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an irreversible reaction?

options.text: The thermal decomposition of ammonium chloride
The Haber process for making ammonia

questions.explanation: Combustion of magnesium is irreversible -- once magnesium burns in oxygen to form magnesium oxide, you cannot easily reverse the reaction to get magnesium and oxygen back.

questions.stem: When ammonium chloride is heated, it breaks down into ammonia and hydrogen chloride. When cooled, the gases recombine. What type of system would prevent equilibrium from being reached?

options.text: An open system where the gases can escape

questions.explanation: In an open system, the gases (ammonia and hydrogen chloride) can escape. If they leave the system, the reverse reaction cannot occur, so equilibrium is never reached.

questions.stem: In a reversible reaction, what determines which direction is favoured?

options.text: The conditions such as temperature and pressure
The size of the container only

questions.explanation: The direction favoured in a reversible reaction depends on the conditions, including temperature, pressure, and concentration of reactants and products.
